body.x: Raion Robotics Inc. (CEO Hwangbo JeMin) has announced its participation in CES 2025, which will occur in Las Vegas from January 7 to 10. The company will present its cutting-edge technologies in the “K-Startup Pavilion.”

Raion Robotics specializes in robotics design and locomotion technology. Its flagship quadruped robot, “Raibo,” is designed to perform land-based missions in environments difficult for humans to navigate, advancing unmanned solutions for challenging terrains.

At CES 2025, Raion Robotics will unveil its second-generation model, Raibo 2. This quadruped robot showcases the company’s ability to design core components such as motors, motor drivers, and gearboxes in-house.

Raibo 2 is engineered to navigate irregular terrains such as stairs, dense foliage, steep slopes, and mountain paths with stability and precision. Leveraging advanced robotic control technology and deep reinforcement learning, the robot combines dynamic performance and durability, reaching speeds of up to 4 meters per second.

With a fully charged battery, Raibo 2 can operate for up to 8 hours, making it suitable for various tasks, including autonomous patrols in border areas, last-mile delivery in urban settings, and long-distance missions. Raion Robotics aims to use Raibo 2’s versatile capabilities to highlight its expertise in robotics and software design while expanding its presence in the global robotics industry.

body.cap: Raibo 2 in different terrains | Photo by RAION Robotics

body.x: “Raibo 2 recently became the first quadruped robot to complete a full marathon (42.195 km), overcoming longstanding limitations in range and operational duration,” a company representative noted. “This achievement demonstrates its potential in diverse environments and showcases the robot’s superior design and functionality. CES 2025 offers the perfect platform to share these successes with a global audience.”

The company also plans to use CES to explore new markets worldwide, building on its recent sales agreement with a Singapore-based firm. “We are confident that Raibo 2’s broad applications and stable performance will open new distribution channels in North America, Europe, Northeast Asia, and the Middle East,” the representative added.

AVING News, which has covered CES for 19 consecutive years, continues to bridge the gap for Korean SMEs and startups looking to expand globally. To promote Korean startups worldwide, AVING will host its Broadcasting Zone at the Venetian Expo, featuring the CES Media Day Startup Conference and global media interviews. AVING’s international media partners will cover these programs.
Following CES 2025, AVING will co-host review conferences with participating companies in Korea, offering a platform for increased visibility and improved corporate image.
